title: Ansys Optics — STL import: Simulation object
claim: STL represents surface triangles, imports as planar solids, lacks length units, and requires separate material assignment; ASCII/binary and facet count tradeoffs.

title: HDF Group — Chunking in HDF5
claim: HDF5 stores multidimensional datasets using contiguous or chunked layouts; chunks permit partial access. Container/layout differs from geometry representation.

title: Khronos — glTF 2.0 Specification
claim: glTF geometry, scene structure, metre units, right-handed coordinates and PBR rendering material semantics; these are not a complete dispersive electromagnetic constitutive model.

title: Stanford Computer Graphics Laboratory — The Stanford 3D Scanning Repository
claim: Raw range scans and reconstructed meshes differ; reconstruction can remove noise and encode connectivity, and PLY is used for these datasets.

title: CGAL — Polygon Mesh Processing User Manual
claim: Polygon mesh validity, self-intersection checks, closed-mesh inside/outside queries, and surface-distance tools are distinct geometry operations.

title: Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys — PBRT: Triangle Meshes
claim: Indexed shared vertices reduce repeated position storage; interpolated shading normals differ from triangle geometric shape.

title: Wavefront — Object Files (.obj), original specification archive
claim: Original OBJ specification supports polygonal and free-form geometry. Search-indexed primary document verified; direct retrieval was blocked/timed out.

title: RIT DIRSIG — Alias/Wavefront OBJ File Format
claim: Vertex/face indexing, material identifiers and the limitations of MTL material descriptions for a physical simulation application.

title: VTK — vtkPLYReader Class Reference
claim: PLY vertices, face indices and supported scalar/colour/texture properties; supported property semantics depend on reader implementation.

title: Kitware VTK — vtkSTLWriter.cxx
claim: Primary implementation of binary STL header, count, normal, three vertices and attribute storage, supporting the 84+50F byte calculation.

title: Open CASCADE Technology — Introduction: Modeling Data
claim: B-Rep combines mathematical geometry with topology; supported geometric types include canonical surfaces and NURBS.

title: Open CASCADE Technology — Modeling Data
claim: Curve and surface interpolation versus approximation; geometric and topological data structures.

title: Open CASCADE Technology — STEP Translator
claim: STEP exchanges geometry, topology and assembly data; extended attributes are handled separately from the basic shape translator.

title: OpenSCAD — Official CheatSheet
claim: Solid primitives, transformations and union/difference/intersection provide a concrete CSG example.

title: VTK — VTK File Formats, version 9.5.2 documentation
claim: Structured points, rectilinear and unstructured grids; explicit distinction between POINT_DATA and CELL_DATA.

title: Ju, Losasso, Schaefer and Warren (2002) — Dual Contouring of Hermite Data
claim: Hermite edge-intersection and normal information enables contouring with additional boundary constraints and octree-based simplification.

title: Schwarz and Seidel (2010) — Fast Parallel Surface and Solid Voxelization on GPUs
claim: Conservative surface versus solid voxelization; sparse octree representation uses fine boundary voxels and coarse uniform interior/exterior regions.

title: OpenVDB — Overview
claim: Hierarchical sparse tree, transform and metadata separation; constant tiles and narrow-band level-set semantics.

title: OpenVDB — NanoVDB FAQ
claim: NanoVDB has static tree topology but values may be modified; contiguous pointerless layout supports CPU/GPU access.

title: Osher and Fedkiw — Level Set Methods, author-hosted manuscript
claim: Interfaces are represented as zero level sets of a scalar function; distance reinitialization and narrow-band methods are distinct numerical operations.

title: Gmsh — Reference Manual: Mesh module and x2 terrain/hybrid example
claim: Surface and volume meshing, tetrahedral/hexahedral/prismatic elements, conformity and terrain/discrete/hybrid geometries.

title: MFEM — Electromagnetics Mini Applications
claim: Finite-element electromagnetic applications have material constitutive relations and discretization requirements separate from geometry files.

title: MFEM — Example Codes and Miniapps
claim: Finite-element spaces, Maxwell examples and DG advection with face integrators illustrate solver discretizations beyond Yee FDTD.

title: Park et al. (2019) — DeepSDF: Learning Continuous Signed Distance Functions for Shape Representation
claim: A learned SDF encodes surface through its zero level set and inside/outside through its sign.

title: Mildenhall et al. (2020) — NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
claim: Original NeRF maps spatial location and viewing direction to volume density and emitted radiance for view synthesis; it is not directly a silicon permittivity field.

title: Kerbl et al. (2023) — 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
claim: Optimized 3D Gaussians represent radiance fields for real-time novel-view rendering, with objectives different from electromagnetic material-boundary validation.

title: Lorensen and Cline (1987) — Marching Cubes: A High Resolution 3D Surface Construction Algorithm
claim: Case-table contouring with interpolation constructs triangular isosurfaces from sampled scalar volume data.

title: Lewiner et al. — Efficient implementation of marching cubes cases with topological guarantees
claim: Ambiguous marching-cubes cases need topology-aware handling; guarantees concern the assumed scalar-field interpolation rather than unknown physical truth.

title: Pharr, Jakob and Humphreys — PBRT: Bounding Volume Hierarchies
claim: BVHs partition primitives into hierarchical bounding boxes to skip irrelevant intersection tests at additional construction/memory cost.

title: CGAL — Fast Intersection and Distance Computation: AABB Tree
claim: AABB tree supports ray/intersection and distance queries and documents tree construction and traversal.

title: Garland and Heckbert (1997) — Surface Simplification Using Quadric Error Metrics
claim: Iterative vertex-pair contraction uses approximate quadric plane-distance costs, not a universal Hausdorff or electromagnetic-error bound.

title: CGAL — Triangulated Surface Mesh Simplification User Manual
claim: Cost, placement, stop predicates and additional filters are distinct; polyhedral-envelope filtering adds constraints beyond raw QEM cost.

title: h5py — Datasets
claim: Chunked storage and lossless filters differ from lossy scale-offset; chunk access affects data movement and memory.
